content.text:
You are building an admin product catalog page for an e-commerce team.

The catalog is read-heavy and should feel fast for day-to-day browsing, so avoid re-querying product data on every request.

Admins can trigger a "Sync latest catalog" action from the page when upstream ERP/PIM data changes (pricing, inventory, availability). After submitting, they should be able to continue working immediately, even if the product list is briefly stale.

The expected behavior is that product data is refreshed in the background and becomes up to date shortly after, across any views that depend on the same catalog data.

Implement the sync trigger as a regular HTML form that uses an inline Server Action in the page.
Use the cache tag name `"products"` consistently for catalog caching and invalidation.

In practice, sync jobs can touch thousands of SKUs, so operators prioritize a responsive admin experience and eventual consistency across catalog views over forcing every request to block on freshly recomputed data.

+import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
 
+/** Cache tag for all catalog reads; use with `revalidateTag` after upstream changes. */
+export const PRODUCTS_CACHE_TAG = 'products' as const
+
+export type Product = {
+  id: number
+  sku: string
+  name: string
+  price: number
+}
+
+type CatalogPayload = {
+  products: Product[]
+  /** Monotonic generation bumped after each simulated ERP/PIM sync completes. */
+  generation: number
+  lastSyncCompletedAt: string | null
+}
+
+const BASE_PRODUCTS: Product[] = [
+  { id: 1, sku: 'ELEC-LAP-01', name: 'Laptop', price: 999 },
+  { id: 2, sku: 'ELEC-PHN-02', name: 'Phone', price: 699 },
+  { id: 3, sku: 'ELEC-TAB-03', name: 'Tablet', price: 499 },
+  { id: 4, sku: 'ACC-HDP-04', name: 'Headphones', price: 199 },
+  { id: 5, sku: 'ACC-WCH-05', name: 'Watch', price: 299 },
+]
+
+let catalogGeneration = 0
+let lastSyncCompletedAt: string | null = null
+
+/**
+ * Simulated ERP/PIM pull — in production this would batch thousands of SKUs
+ * and write through to your database or search index.
+ */
+export async function syncCatalogFromUpstream(): Promise<void> {
+  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1200))
+  catalogGeneration += 1
+  lastSyncCompletedAt = new Date().toISOString()
+}
+
+async function loadCatalogFromSource(): Promise<CatalogPayload> {
+  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100))
+  return {
+    products: BASE_PRODUCTS.map((p) => ({
+      ...p,
+      price: p.price + catalogGeneration,
+    })),
+    generation: catalogGeneration,
+    lastSyncCompletedAt,
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Shared catalog read for admin surfaces. Tagged so `revalidateTag(PRODUCTS_CACHE_TAG, …)`
+ * can refresh all dependent routes without re-querying on every navigation.
+ */
+export const getCachedProductCatalog = unstable_cache(
+  async () => loadCatalogFromSource(),
+  ['admin-product-catalog'],
+  { tags: [PRODUCTS_CACHE_TAG] }
+)

content.text:
Here is what was implemented.

### Behavior

- **Cached reads** — `getCachedProductCatalog()` in `lib/catalog.ts` wraps the (simulated) catalog load with `unstable_cache` and the tag **`"products"`**, so normal navigations reuse the Data Cache instead of hitting the “source” on every request.
- **Sync without blocking** — The catalog page uses a **plain `<form action={…}>`** whose handler is an **inline Server Action**. It schedules work with **`after()`** from `next/server`: when the request finishes, `syncCatalogFromUpstream()` runs (simulated ~1.2s ERP/PIM job), then **`revalidateTag(PRODUCTS_CACHE_TAG, 'max')`** so the tag is refreshed with a **stale-while-revalidate–style** profile (aligned with Next’s cache-life `"max"` semantics). The submit returns right away so admins can keep working; the list may stay slightly stale until that work completes.
- **Shared catalog views** — `/admin/catalog/summary` calls the same `getCachedProductCatalog()`, so both routes stay aligned once the tag revalidates.

### Files

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| [`lib/catalog.ts`](lib/catalog.ts) | `PRODUCTS_CACHE_TAG`, `getCachedProductCatalog`, `syncCatalogFromUpstream` |
| [`app/admin/layout.tsx`](app/admin/layout.tsx) | Admin chrome + `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` so catalog isn’t frozen at build time |
| [`app/admin/catalog/page.tsx`](app/admin/catalog/page.tsx) | Grid UI, sync form, inline `requestCatalogSync` server action |
| [`app/admin/catalog/summary/page.tsx`](app/admin/catalog/summary/page.tsx) | Second view using the same cache |

### Replacing the demo with production

- Point `loadCatalogFromSource()` at your DB/API instead of the in-memory demo.
- Implement `syncCatalogFromUpstream()` as your real batch job (or enqueue a worker); keep **`revalidateTag('products', 'max')`** (or adjust the profile) **after** persisted data is updated so readers don’t flash half-applied state.

`npm run build` completes successfully; admin routes render dynamically (`ƒ`).

Forcing dynamic rendering for admin routes so the catalog isn't frozen at build time and sync + `unstable_cache` behave correctly at runtime.








Here is what was implemented.

### Behavior

- **Cached reads** — `getCachedProductCatalog()` in `lib/catalog.ts` wraps the (simulated) catalog load with `unstable_cache` and the tag **`"products"`**, so normal navigations reuse the Data Cache instead of hitting the “source” on every request.
- **Sync without blocking** — The catalog page uses a **plain `<form action={…}>`** whose handler is an **inline Server Action**. It schedules work with **`after()`** from `next/server`: when the request finishes, `syncCatalogFromUpstream()` runs (simulated ~1.2s ERP/PIM job), then **`revalidateTag(PRODUCTS_CACHE_TAG, 'max')`** so the tag is refreshed with a **stale-while-revalidate–style** profile (aligned with Next’s cache-life `"max"` semantics). The submit returns right away so admins can keep working; the list may stay slightly stale until that work completes.
- **Shared catalog views** — `/admin/catalog/summary` calls the same `getCachedProductCatalog()`, so both routes stay aligned once the tag revalidates.

### Files

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| [`lib/catalog.ts`](lib/catalog.ts) | `PRODUCTS_CACHE_TAG`, `getCachedProductCatalog`, `syncCatalogFromUpstream` |
| [`app/admin/layout.tsx`](app/admin/layout.tsx) | Admin chrome + `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` so catalog isn’t frozen at build time |
| [`app/admin/catalog/page.tsx`](app/admin/catalog/page.tsx) | Grid UI, sync form, inline `requestCatalogSync` server action |
| [`app/admin/catalog/summary/page.tsx`](app/admin/catalog/summary/page.tsx) | Second view using the same cache |

### Replacing the demo with production

- Point `loadCatalogFromSource()` at your DB/API instead of the in-memory demo.
- Implement `syncCatalogFromUpstream()` as your real batch job (or enqueue a worker); keep **`revalidateTag('products', 'max')`** (or adjust the profile) **after** persisted data is updated so readers don’t flash half-applied state.

`npm run build` completes successfully; admin routes render dynamically (`ƒ`).
